turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Mrs Naidoo? Come through, the doctor's just finishing. Your partner can wait on the chairs for a bit.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, alright. I'm absolutely shattered, so if we can not make a whole morning of this.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Shame. I'll do the observations quickly. Blood pressure is one eighteen over seventy four, pulse is eighty six, temperature thirty six point seven.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. They already did a urine test at the desk and said it's positive, so I don't know why we're starting from scratch.
[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Ja, that urine pregnancy test was positive this morning. Any allergies I should put on the form before the doctor comes?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None. I told the other lady that already.
[SEG0007] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): No known allergies, got it. I'll send Doctor in. Just shout if you want your partner.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello, I'm Doctor Pillay. You look done in. What's brought you today?

[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm pregnant, somewhere around eight to ten weeks I think, and now I'm spotting, and I've got cramps. I just need to know the baby is okay. I'm sick of sitting here worrying.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Spotting and cramps. When did the bleeding actually start?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Yesterday morning. It's brown, and a bit pink when I wipe. Not like a period. I'm not soaking a pad.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the cramps, did they come on with the spotting?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Since yesterday, low down, on and off. Not the worst pain I've had, but it's sore. I took two Panado this morning and it eased a bit.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright. Any fainting, any fever, or pain right at the tip of the shoulder?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No faint, no fever, no shoulder pain. I was queasy last night. I didn't vomit, before you write that down.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nausea without vomiting, okay. Can you date the last period at all?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Um. The last period was around Diwali, or after. I can't pin the day. Could've been the week after, the month was hectic, I honestly don't know.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): If it was around Diwali you'd land near eight to ten weeks, and if it was after that you might be earlier. I'm not going to pretend we can date it off that. The scan can.

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): I've been anxious the whole week, and I can't sleep properly. And no, I don't smoke, I never have. I stay with my partner, he's outside, probably annoying whoever's on the desk.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Worry and broken sleep on top of the rest, ja. What medicines are you actually taking?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Folic acid, five milligrams, every morning, since the test turned positive. And I stopped the Triphasil in March. The pill. I haven't touched it since.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Folic acid five milligrams every morning, and the Triphasil stopped in March. Did they give you anything for the nausea?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Cyclizine. The clinic wrote it weeks ago. I never took it, the box is still sealed in the cupboard, so don't put me down as on it.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): We won't. Cyclizine never started. Any operations, or any illness that's still going?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No operations. Nothing ongoing. Can he come in? If he sits out there he'll interrogate me in the car, and I haven't got the energy.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ja, let's bring him in.
[SEG0027] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): He's just here. Come through, sir.
[SEG0028] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thanks. She's been sore on and off for about two weeks, not just from yesterday. She's been holding her stomach since the weekend before last.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): That's not right. The cramps started yesterday, same as the spotting. Maybe a niggle the night before, but it is not two weeks. Don't speak for me.
[SEG0030] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): You were complaining last week. I'm not making it up.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): I was tired last week. Tired is not cramps. I'm tired now as well, so can we please get on with it.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): You two aren't going to settle that in here. I'll put the cramps down as somewhere between about a day and two weeks, and we'll treat the timing as not exact.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me feel your tummy. It's soft, a little tender low down in the middle, no guarding, and no pain when I press over the sides.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, that's the spot. It's not agony, so don't poke.

[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): I won't do an internal exam. Thinking it through, spotting with cramps this early is most often a threatened miscarriage, but an ectopic can look the same, and I can't separate the two without a scan.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): So you think it's in the tube? Just say it properly. I'm too tired for hints.

[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): I don't think that. I can't exclude it. So today, not next week: a scan on this side, and bloods, the pregnancy hormone, a full blood count, and your group and antibodies, the rhesus especially.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): All of that today? I'm supposed to be back at work.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Today, yes. The scan is booked just now, and we'll take the bloods before you leave these rooms. I'll go through the results with you later today.
[SEG0040] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She hasn't really eaten either. Hardly any breakfast.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): I had toast. Don't turn it into a thing. I'm nauseous, I'm not starving myself.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Toast is enough. Little and often if the nausea stays. For pain, stick with Panado, not ibuprofen or the other anti-inflammatories.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): I already had two. The five hundred milligram ones. It took the edge off, that's all.
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's a gram, that's a fine dose. No sex until we've seen the scan, and no heavy lifting today. Just take it easy.
[SEG0045] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And if it gets worse while we're waiting on the scan, where do we actually go?
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the bleeding gets heavier, or you get shoulder pain, or you feel faint, come straight back. Casualty if these rooms are closed. You don't wait until the morning.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Heavier, like a pad?
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Soaking through a pad in an hour, or clots, or pain that Panado isn't touching. That's when you come back. No debating it.
[SEG0049] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll make sure she does. She puts things off.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm sitting right here. I don't put things off, I'm exhausted. There's a difference.
[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): Heard. The plan is the scan and the bloods now, and I will see you later today with whatever they show.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): And if my dates are rubbish?
[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): Then we go by the size on the scan, and by the hormone if it's too early to see much. I am not locking eight to ten weeks to a period you can't date.
[SEG0054] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I can take her for the bloods now. The scan slot is in about twenty minutes, and her partner can walk up with her.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. Let's just do it. I want to go and lie down after.
[SEG0056] person_3 (DOCTOR): Go with sister. And once more, so it's clear: heavier bleeding, shoulder pain, or feeling faint, you come straight back.
